subject.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled

question: Should cron-owned main-session systemEvent wakes bypass per-agent heartbeat disabled/omitted scheduler gates while preserving the global heartbeat disable gate?
rationale: This PR's cron-layer preservation does not make the deferred wake deliver under current disabled gates, and deciding whether cron scheduling overrides per-agent heartbeat omission is a compatibility/product policy choice.

options.title: Repair at heartbeat boundary
options.body: Accept cron as the owner of these wakes, preserve the global disable gate, fix both direct and queued heartbeat gates, and require real cron proof before merge.

options.title: Keep per-agent disable authoritative
options.body: Require cron to report skipped/error without retaining unreachable events when per-agent heartbeat policy prevents delivery.

options.title: Use the sibling candidate
options.body: Pause this PR and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101584 as the heartbeat-boundary fix after proof and maintainer acceptance.

recommendation.title: Repair at heartbeat boundary
recommendation.body: Accept cron as the owner of these wakes, preserve the global disable gate, fix both direct and queued heartbeat gates, and require real cron proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work spans the cron dispatch and heartbeat summary/gate surfaces involved in the compatibility choice.
